# HumanPush

> In development. No real orders or payments run yet. AI agents will request the work and the signature of a professional listed in a public Dutch register through HumanPush. The company pays 100% upfront. The signed work comes back with proof that anyone can check independently.

People use https://humanpush.nl. This file is for agents and lives at https://humanpush.nl/llms.txt.

What works now is the sandbox, with pretend money and a pretend register. Production starts after the test phase is completed. There is no start date yet. Netherlands first, companies only (B2B, with a Dutch KvK number).

HumanPush is a trade name of Humagent B.V., KvK [KVK-NUMMER].

## Sandbox

- Get a key: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/
- MCP endpoint: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/mcp
- The endpoint asks for the sandbox key.
- Public keys for the signatures: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/.well-known/humanpush-keys.json

The public sandbox still runs an earlier test version of the protocol. Where it differs from the rules below, the rules below are the ones being built for the start. The differences: the sandbox still has a 50% cancellation step, a repair round after a dispute, reassignment to another professional after acceptance, and an Rbtv sworn translator in its catalog. The sandbox clock runs faster than real time, so poll get_status.

## What it does

An agent asks a registered professional to do the work and sign it. HumanPush checks the registration in the public register. It does not judge the quality of the work. It is not part of any of the registers.

Five services at the start, one per register:

- NIVRE: nivre.independent_opinion. An independent opinion on a claims decision, on the documents only. No inspection on site, no personal injury at the start.
- NRVT: a valuation of a home by a registered valuer of the Kamer Wonen, not NWWI. Not for a mortgage or NHG.
- NRGD: nrgd.multimedia_authenticity. Whether an image or video shows signs of manipulation, by a court expert in multimedia forensics (008.4). Outside court proceedings; not a court expert report.
- OCNL: ocnl.novelty_quickscan. A novelty quick scan by a patent attorney. No filing, no freedom-to-operate opinion. The professional sees which company asks, for the mandatory conflict check.
- NRBI: nrbi.report_desk_review. A remote review of an existing building inspection report for an existing home. Not a new inspection.

Not offered: sworn translators (Rbtv, parked), notaries (KNB) and bailiffs (KBvG).

Under the AVG (article 22) a person can have a right to human intervention in certain decisions based solely on automated processing. HumanPush is how an agent asks a registered professional to do that work and sign it.

## When to use HumanPush

- A decision or report needs a registered professional to do the work and sign it, and the service is one of the five above.
- You must rely on that signature and need proof that can be checked independently.

## When not to use HumanPush

- The work does not need a registered signer.
- You want a judgement of quality. HumanPush checks registration, not quality.
- Notarial deeds, bailiff work, sworn translations.
- Consumers. HumanPush is for companies.

## The rules (as decided for the start)

The protocol runs the terms; the log is the proof. If the terms, the protocol and this file differ, the terms come first, then the protocol, then this file. Time limits and amounts are working rules or test values during the test phase, not fixed facts.

- Every step by a professional or reviewer is a signed action with a passkey. There is no sign-off by an e-mail code.
- A professional has 4 working hours to accept or decline. Declining never counts against him; the request goes to the next professional of the register. Accepting binds both sides.
- Cancel: free until the professional accepts. After that, until delivery, 25% of the professional's fee goes to the professional (a test value, not yet fixed) and the rest is refunded. There is no 50% step.
- If nobody accepts, the professional withdraws after accepting, or he delivers late, the company gets everything back. There is no replacement after acceptance and no extension.
- Conflict of interest: only for a service with a mandatory conflict check (now OCNL), the professional can return an accepted order before delivery. The company gets everything back, with no cancellation fee. The professional gets no failure but a mark; 3 marks within 12 months count as 1 failure. A reviewer who reports a conflict gets the same mark instead of a failure.
- After delivery the company has 72 hours to accept or dispute. Silence counts as accept.
- A dispute can only name the fixed review criteria of the service, such as form_complete and question_answered. Wanting a different conclusion is not a ground. A second professional of the same register reviews only those criteria. The verdict is binary: meets or fails. A fails verdict must name the ground. Meets: the professional is paid. Fails: the company gets everything back. There is no repair after delivery and no partial outcome.
- If the register reports the professional as suspended or deregistered, an order that is not yet delivered stops and the company gets everything back. Work already delivered runs on. NIVRE, NRVT and OCNL show no suspension; there only a deregistration counts.

## Registration proof

- The floor is proof level 2. A company can ask for a higher level per order, never a lower one.
- HumanPush checks the registration against the public register and records a register attestation with a validity period: 30 days, and for OCNL also a list reference date of at most 120 days. The register is checked again at every acceptance; for NRVT that check is manual and logged.
- The attestation shows what the register said at the check. It does not prove the live state of the register.

## Tools (sandbox, earlier test version)

These are the calls of the public sandbox. They run on pretend data and pretend money. A write call takes an idempotency_key. The same key does not run the action twice.

Usual order: list_services, then request_signoff, then poll get_status. After a delivery: respond_to_result, then get_result, then verify_proof. Upload documents with create_upload_url when the work needs files. Read the log with get_events, or take it with you using export_request.

### list_services

Return the fixed catalog of services per register, with terms, a price range, lead times and the professionals who offer each service. Call this before request_signoff.

- input: register, profession, region or language, all optional.
- output: services, each with a service_id, the terms, a price range and the professionals
- price: Price on request
- sandbox: pretend catalog, free

### verify_professional

Return a signed register attestation for one person in one register: what the register said at the check, with a validity period. It is not a live reading of the register.

- input: register and registration_number. as_of is optional. The sandbox register has no history.
- output: registered true or false, the status, and a signed attestation
- sandbox: pretend register, free

### create_upload_url

Get a one-time URL and upload one document with HTTP PUT (raw bytes). Pass the document_id to request_signoff.

- input: idempotency_key, filename, content_type, size_bytes, and the sha256 of the file
- output: document_id, upload_url, method PUT, expires_at
- files: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, PNG or JPG, up to 20 MB. The sha256 must match the bytes.

### request_signoff

Ask a registered professional to do a service and sign it. The company pays 100% up front: the professional's fee plus the HumanPush fee.

- input: idempotency_key, service_id, task, and deadline (ISO 8601, at most 30 working days ahead). Optional: document_ids, professional_id, and the options of the earlier test version for an unavailable professional.
- output: review_id, status, the deadlines, the amount, and in the sandbox a pay page
- price: Price on request
- sandbox: pretend money, free

### get_status

Current status, the deadlines, and the next action.

- input: review_id from request_signoff
- output: status, next_action, the deadlines, payment, is_final

### respond_to_result

After delivery, accept or dispute. Silence for 72 hours counts as accept. The earlier test version in the sandbox still gives a repair round on the first dispute; the rules above have none.

- input: idempotency_key, review_id, and action (accept or dispute). Optional: reason.
- output: the updated status

### cancel_signoff

Cancel. Free until the professional accepts. Under the rules above, 25% of the professional's fee after that, until delivery. The earlier test version in the sandbox still has a 50% step.

- input: idempotency_key, review_id, reason
- output: status cancelled, the fee kept, and the refund

### get_result

The outcome, the signed result, and once it is final the proof. Pass that proof to verify_proof, or to anyone who needs to check it.

- input: review_id
- output: the signed result and the proof. Before a delivery, the call reports that nothing has been delivered yet.

### get_events

The signed, hash-chained events of one review, oldest first. Use since_seq to fetch only new ones.

- input: review_id, and since_seq if you only want events after that sequence number
- output: events, each with a hash, the previous hash, a signature, and an actor signature

### export_request

Export one review as JSON: the signed event chain, the signatures and the public keys. The same document is GET /reviews/{review_id}/export on the sandbox, with the sandbox key.

- input: review_id
- output: the export. Check it offline with npm run verify -- <export.json>

### verify_proof

Check a HumanPush proof yourself: the signature and every event hash and signature.

- input: the proof object from get_result
- output: valid true or false, and the problems when it does not check out
- keys: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/.well-known/humanpush-keys.json

## Payment

- The company pays 100% upfront: the professional's fee plus the HumanPush fee. The HumanPush fee is price on request.
- The professional is paid after acceptance or after the 72-hour dispute window.
- No real payments run yet. Sandbox: pretend money, free.

## Proof

Every final result includes verifiable proof of who signed, when, and which register attestation applied then. The proof is the signed hash chain. Anyone can check that proof independently. export_request is that chain in one file, and the file can be checked offline.
